final_proof:
Let \(X\) be the point set, with \(|X|=v\), and let \(\mathcal B\) be the collection of blocks, with \(|\mathcal B|=b\). Thus every block has size \(k\), and every pair of distinct points is contained in exactly \(\lambda\) blocks. As usual for a BIBD, the parameters are nontrivial: \(1<k<v\) and \(\lambda>0\).

First we determine how many blocks contain a given point. Fix \(x\in X\), and let \(r_x\) denote the number of blocks containing \(x\). Count pairs \((y,B)\) such that \(y\in X\setminus\{x\}\) and \(B\in\mathcal B\) contains both \(x\) and \(y\). Counting first by blocks containing \(x\) gives \(r_x(k-1)\); counting first by the choice of \(y\) gives \(\lambda(v-1)\). Hence
\[
r_x(k-1)=\lambda(v-1).
\]
In particular, \(r_x\) is independent of \(x\); denote its common value by \(r\). Moreover,
\[
r-\lambda=\frac{\lambda(v-1)}{k-1}-\lambda=\frac{\lambda(v-k)}{k-1}>0.
\]

Now form the \(v\times b\) incidence matrix \(N\), whose \((x,B)\)-entry equals \(1\) if \(x\in B\) and \(0\) otherwise. The diagonal entries of \(NN^{\mathsf T}\) are \(r\), since each point belongs to \(r\) blocks. Its off-diagonal entries are \(\lambda\), since each pair of distinct points belongs to exactly \(\lambda\) blocks. Therefore
\[
NN^{\mathsf T}=(r-\lambda)I_v+\lambda J_v,
\]
where \(I_v\) is the identity matrix and \(J_v\) is the all-ones matrix.

For every nonzero vector \(z\in\mathbb R^v\),
\[
z^{\mathsf T}NN^{\mathsf T}z=(r-\lambda)\sum_{x\in X}z_x^2+\lambda\left(\sum_{x\in X}z_x\right)^2>0,
\]
because \(r-\lambda>0\) and \(\lambda>0\). Thus \(NN^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite and consequently has rank \(v\). On the other hand,
\[
v=\operatorname{rank}(NN^{\mathsf T})\le \operatorname{rank}(N)\le b,
\]
because \(N\) has \(b\) columns. Therefore \(b\ge v\), as claimed.
